source.title: Invariance Makes LLM Unlearning Resilient Even to Unanticipated Downstream Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Chang-Sheng Wang; Yihua Zhang; Jing-Han Jia; Parikshit Ram; Dennis Wei; Yuguang Yao; Soumyadeep Pal; Nathalie Baracaldo; Si-Jia Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study directly tests whether downstream fine-tuning restores performance on unlearned content, and whether ILU and other robust-unlearning methods prevent that recovery. It uses its own unlearning methods and robustness measures rather than reproducing the cited original attack studies.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses cited findings about unrelated fine-tuning, quantization and other attacks, but those cited results are not rows. It reports task-vector cosines as an explanation of its method; those are not direct measurements of recovery. Rows below cover its own fine-tuning and relearning results, including reported aggregate metrics and selected MUSE results.
record.test_reason: The study measures forget quality on WMDP and MUSE before and after downstream fine-tuning and a forget-set relearning attack. NPO and RMU baselines bear on B and on A. Its own ILU method, plus the SAM, LAT and TAR comparators, bear on F. It uses a different protocol from the originals (six unrelated fine-tuning tasks, 60-sample relearning), so T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that NPO and RMU lose forgetting under downstream fine-tuning, even on unrelated tasks, and under relearning. ILU, regularized on one unrelated dataset, improves robustness that generalizes to unseen tasks, while preserving utility. They add that SAM variants resist relearning better than ILU, and that ILU matches TAR's robustness at about 63× less compute. The record omits these two caveats.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes ILU, an invariance regularization added to NPO or RMU, and evaluates downstream fine-tuning and relearning. It does not reproduce the cited original attack methods as its primary intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Robustness varies with unlearning method, invariance dataset, number of invariance datasets, fine-tuning task and regularization parameter λ. The paper reports that a single unrelated invariance dataset can outperform ILU(WMDP) and ILU(Multi); large λ can compromise forget quality, while too-small λ can fail to promote resilience.

fits_no_version.finding: Task-vector cosines: NPO's post-fine-tune update opposes its unlearning direction (cos −0.41), whereas ILU's stays near-orthogonal (0.09).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning recovery occurs because post-unlearning updates move weights back against the unlearning task vector.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 267, 2025
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the tabulated results. The study does not establish a near-chance threshold for its FQ results, and most robustness experiments are on specified tasks and models. Its findings do not test internal edits, quantization or prompt-only attacks.
record.rows_left_out: The full per-task RA/FA entries in Table 2 and Table 4, most per-task MUSE-News and MUSE-Books entries in Table A1, and additional heatmap and figure results are not individually tabulated here; selected aggregate and explicitly discussed conditions were retained to stay within the row limit.

untested.parts: Loosely related relearning sets, and set sizes other than 60 forget samples.
All. The task-vector cosine analysis is not activation ablation.
Robustness of ILU, TAR, LAT and SAM to ablation, quantization and prompting attacks.

missing.what: Per-task final-epoch FQ heatmaps: RMU falls from 0.68 to 0.36–0.38 on all six tasks, NPO from 0.52 to 0.42–0.45. ILU variants are also shown, including the weaker ILU(WMDP).

MUSE-Books results: NPO KnowMem on the forget set rises from 0.00 to about 32–38 after fine-tuning (original 59.40). ILU rises from 0.00 to about 14–31. ILU has a lower retain KnowMem pre-fine-tune (45.20 vs 57.19).
Sensitivity to λ: λ>0.1 lowers forget quality, while λ=0.05 fails to give robustness.
Fine-tuning trajectories showing NPO and RMU FQ converging to the original model's level as epochs increase.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V1/V2/V6 codes map to A/B/F. RA rows wrongly use the original model's RA as baseline; recovery should be judged against pre-fine-tune FQ. FQ = 1 − WMDP-Bio accuracy, with 4-choice chance at FQ 0.75. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The MUSE table text is scrambled in extraction, so the Books numbers are approximate.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not establish that targeted accuracy is near chance, and it does not test ablation, quantization or prompt-only attacks.
It tests downstream task fine-tuning and a relearning attack using 60 forget-set instances for 1 epoch; it does not test every type or size of small relearning set named in the claim.
No activation-direction ablation or access-versus-deletion test is reported.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language or in-context-only attack is tested.
Robustness is tested for downstream fine-tuning, including the stated relearning attack. Robustness to internal edits, quantization and prompting attacks is not tested.

relation.reason: Its results on NPO/RMU baselines and on ILU, SAM, LAT and TAR bear on versions A, B and F.

tranche.reason: Different method (ILU, its own relearning and downstream fine-tuning protocol) aimed at the same question. It measures NPO/RMU recovery and counter-method robustness.

source_check.notes: FQ = 1 - WMDP-Bio accuracy. RA = mean FQ at three fine-tuning milestones, averaged over six full downstream fine-tuning runs to convergence (set sizes not stated, so not 'small' relearning sets). Final-epoch FQ: RMU 0.36-0.38 (Fig. 3), NPO 0.42-0.45 (Fig. A2). Table A1 is garbled but placeable: MUSE-Books ILU KnowMem on Df goes 0 -> 14-31, with no row. TAR and LAT were re-run by the authors.

statements.correction: Zephyr-7B-beta NPO (WMDP-Bio): FQ 0.52 (accuracy about 0.48) vs original FQ 0.36; MMLU 58.15 -> 56.69 (Table 2).

statements.correction: Zephyr-7B-beta NPO: RA 0.47 from FQ 0.52, original 0.37 (final-epoch FQ 0.42-0.45, Fig. A2). LLaMA3-8B-Instruct NPO: RA 0.61 from 0.73, original 0.29. Zephyr RMU: RA 0.42 from 0.68, final-epoch 0.36-0.38 vs original 0.36 (Fig. 3).
statements.problem: Cites r10/r17 under a 'challenges' entry. They show partial recovery (verdict limits_scope), and the same study finds near-full RMU recovery from the same unrelated tasks.

statements.correction: Zephyr-7B-beta NPO: average RA 0.47 from FQ 0.52, original RA 0.37 (about 33%); final-epoch FQ 0.42-0.45 (Fig. A2). LLaMA3-8B-Instruct NPO: RA 0.61 from 0.73, original 0.29 (about 27%). RA = mean FQ at first-quartile, median and final epochs; 0.47 is the mean over six tasks.
